findings.reason: the verdict for two of the six signals is unimplementable exactly as written, so §33's deliverable ("names every signal that clears that bar, or says that none does") is not definable until the plan says how an unordered signal's two buckets are compared.
findings.text: §33's bar reads "A candidate signal separates a cell ... only when its lowest and highest buckets in that cell meet those same two conditions", but two of the six candidate signals carry no ordering: `node_definition.negative_control` is yes/no (line 252) and the section's own control is the even/odd parity of the run id's timestamp seconds (line 255). The plan handles the unordered case for the control alone ("its two buckets", line 257) and gives no rule for a candidate, so a node implementing §33 cannot compute the bar for those two signals without inventing an ordering the plan never states.

findings.reason: the two readings produce different tables and can yield different separating signals, which is exactly the verdict §34 is deferred on (line 269), so the plan must settle which population it means before the measurement runs.
findings.text: the deliverable defines the population as "the one a pick reads: implement rows over the 14 days to the run", but the same sentence requires every count to be "reported per project, role, spec level and requirement" and the done-when (line 261) keys each table row on "project, role, spec level, requirement, bucket". A pick reads rows at the role its own request names (_candidates_scan compares row role to request.node.role, reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:327-331), which is not restricted to implement; so the declared population and the declared cell key disagree, and the node must guess whether to filter role == "implement" or to cut by role.

findings.reason: the reader reaches _candidates_scan from the citation either way, so correcting the line number changes nothing a node would build.
findings.text: §33 cites "_candidates_scan (reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:256)", but line 256 is blank and the function is defined at line 257; the same one-line drift appears in §31 (line 181) and §32 (line 209), so the anchor was written against an earlier revision of the module. The symbol still resolves, so the citation is usable, but the line number does not name it.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the anchor for _candidates_scan is one line off the symbol it names.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the separating bar is stated over a signal's "lowest and highest buckets", an ordering two of the six signals do not have.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the document and figures write under docs/research/ and docs/figures/, and the computing script is required by done-when item 3 to sit in the node's own run directory, which is the durable per-run store a later reader can open.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the write paths (docs/research/what-sizes-a-node.html, docs/figures/what-sizes-a-node) are named by behaviour and carry no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §33 declares its population to be implement rows while its done-when keys each table row on role beside project, spec level and requirement, so the section's mechanism does not produce the table its own done-when demands.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §33 carries one deliverable (one research document plus its figures) and one measure, so it can be closed on a single verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s34's depends-on entry naming lane-and-model-routing#s33 is present in plan-section-depends-on (line 22), and §33 itself declares no depends-on because it changes no code and reads only committed ledgers, so it needs no upstream edge.
